children: KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--Malaysia has introduced measures to address rising living costs and support businesses.
Malaysia will raise the monthly basic eligibility limit for subsidized RON95 fuel to 300 liters from 200 liters, effective Sept. 1, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.

The increase will benefit more than 16 million RON95 fuel users, while eligible private diesel pickup and jeep owners can apply for an additional 100 liters, raising their monthly limit to 400 liters, Anwar said Sunday in a televised address for the country's National Day.
The government will also offer three months of free subscriptions to some artificial-intelligence programs to 100,000 Malaysian youths aged 18 to 30 who complete required modules.

The Malaysian government will add 1 billion ringgit, equivalent to $248.4 million, to microfinancing facilities, bringing total funding for 2026 to 6 billion ringgit. The government will also introduce a 200 million ringgit grant for small businesses such as hawkers and home-based businesses.
Authorities also raised the e-invoice exemption threshold to 3 million ringgit in annual sales from 1 million ringgit, easing compliance requirements for small businesses.
